newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP committee to extend BSE inquiry.
newsitem.headline: EP committee to extend BSE inquiry.

text.p: The European Parliament's special committee of inquiry into Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) is set to be extended to February 1997, after its mandate expires on November 17.
"An extra three months will be necessary to complete the work," said Reimer Boge, the committee's German Christian Democrat president in a news release.
A number of points still have to be clarified and more officials will be required to give evidence.
Commissioner Karel Van Miert, formerly responsible for consumer affairs, has accepted to appear before the committee on October 28.
Public Health Commissioner Padraig Flynn has agreed to appear on October 29 while Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, who testified in early September, will appear again on November 4.
Commission Director General for Agriculture, Guy Legras, and the director for animal health, Lars Hoelgaard, have agreed to answer more questions from the committee.
Boge said that British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg had been re-invited to appear before the committee.
Hogg declined an earlier invitation, sending his senior agriculture civil servant Richard Packer, to answer questions.
